Design a 60-90 sprint roadmap to take InkOS from current state (Sprint 12 complete, launch-ready) to full PDF spec compliance. Output is for a plan file, not implementation.

**Current state (audit findings):**
- 16 modules in PDF, 9 fully exist, 5 partial, 2 missing (AI Assist drafts/summary/aftercare; client portal magic link)
- Sprint 12 complete per CLAUDE.md
- 72 migrations, 511 routes, 286 components, 46 tests
- Dodo Payments wired (L1 SaaS billing only)
- Multi-channel inbox webhooks live but channel-tagged UI + AI drafts missing
- 7 of 8 client tabs exist, Financial tab + persistent allergies banner missing
- Photo timeline schema partial (slot_type column added 2026-04-30, but no sessions table — projects infer from bookings)
- /reports exists, named differently than PDF /analytics
- Demo seed exists but generic personas, NOT Maya/Miles/Karisa archetypes from PDF

**Locked decisions:**
- L1 SaaS billing: Dodo Payments (current, MoR for global SaaS tax)
- L2 in-studio billing: Stripe Connect (NEW — destination charges, 70/30 splits, Stripe Tax line items, dispute defense pack auto-bundling, 1099-NEC export)
- Public portfolio: portfolio.inkos.studio/[studio]/[artist] subdomain via wildcard DNS + middleware host rewrite
- 5 InkOS-specific agents: inkos-payments-lead, inkos-inbox-lead, inkos-canvas-lead, inkos-compliance-lead, inkos-brand-guardian

**Critical missing/partial features (from audit):**

Tier 1 — Launch blockers:
1. AI Assist 3 jobs (inbound reply drafts in studio voice, consult-to-3-bullet summary, aftercare auto-gen from session data) with "never sends autonomously" guard
2. Persistent red allergies banner across all 8 client tabs + audit-logged clear/edit
3. Client portal via SMS magic link (project view, deposit pool, photo timeline, next appt, aftercare, consent read-only)
4. 30-min pre-session briefing push (BullMQ worker, allergies + pinned notes + last 3 sessions + deposit pool + outstanding forms)
5. Financial tab on client detail page (8th tab)
6. Stripe Connect L2 marketplace (full payment overhaul — destination charges, deposit pool draw + new charge atomic, commission splits per Stripe Tax line, tip routing, refund proportional reversal)
7. Stripe Tax integration (per-state US tattoo-service tax — NYC 4.5% local, NJ 6.625%, CA/TX/FL/PA exempt for services, Iowa/MA tax permanent makeup, retail line vs service line)
8. 1099-NEC year-end export per artist
9. Dispute defense pack auto-bundling (signed consent + photo release + every session photo + chat history + deposit policy + receipt → one-click Stripe submit)

Tier 2 — Feature completeness:
10. Full kiosk pre-session intake (phone-lookup → 3 forms → single-finger signature → hash + timestamp)
11. Project completion automation (30-day final-healed prompt, photo release confirmation, day-7 review prompt, loyalty credit, 3-month referral, 6-month win-back, birthday card)
12. portfolio.inkos.studio subdomain with wildcard DNS + Enterprise custom domain CNAME
13. Channel-tagged inbox UI (IG/WhatsApp/SMS/Email badges per message)
14. Send Message channel-mismatch warning modal
15. Flash deposit-gated claim (bookable flash with deposit hold)
16. Flash Events full landing pages with public booking widget
17. AI Assist voice-learning (per-artist + per-studio tone learned from prior conversations)
18. Inventory REACH-EU compliance fail-fast at session-start (block session if non-compliant ink for EU client)
19. Tax sub-ledger quarterly export per location
20. Mailchimp segment sync (one-way push from Analytics segments)

Tier 3 — Polish, scale, production hardening:
21. Multi-location consolidated reporting (Enterprise tier)
22. White-label theming (Enterprise tier)
23. Public API + API access (Enterprise tier)
24. SSO for Enterprise
25. Multi-currency (UK GBP, EU EUR, AU AUD with Stripe Connect cross-border)
26. Guest artist invite + 80/20 split + travel/lodging carve-out + auto-deactivate on end date
27. Apprentice workflow (supervised consent, restricted Stripe access, 50/50 ramp split)
28. Studio onboarding wizard (Stripe Connect onboarding, BBP cert upload, state license verification, tax registration)
29. Performance hardening (Lighthouse LCP <2.5s, CLS <0.1 across all 16 modules)
30. Security hardening (re-audit RLS, audit log full coverage, GDPR/CCPA right-to-delete RPC battle-tested)
31. Mobile-first audit (Karisa journey is 100% phone — every flow phone-first)
32. Demo data: Maya/Miles/Karisa personas seeded (replace generic Inkhaus demo with PDF spec personas + 5-session koi sleeve project, allergies banner triggered, deposit pool with mid-project top-up, photo timeline filled)
33. Brand polish: every screen audited against 4 brand rules (editorial polish, rust earned, onyx CTAs, serif moments)
34. NOW sweep bar motion on dashboard timeline (only allowed dashboard motion)
35. Performance: tabular-nums on every number, semantic tokens only, no hex literals in components
36. AI cost monitoring + per-studio cost cap + Pro tier AI quota
37. Internationalization: en-US, en-GB, en-AU, fr, de (per Stripe Connect cross-border markets)
38. Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA across all 16 modules
39. PDF generation: receipts, 1099-NEC, REACH compliance certificates, dispute defense packages
40. Backup/DR: per-studio export (full data dump for studio leaving), automated daily snapshots, point-in-time restore tested

**Required output structure:**

A) **Epic groupings** — group sprints into 8-12 epics. Suggest names like "EPIC 1: Stripe Connect Marketplace (Sprints 13-22)". Each epic gets a 2-line goal + which Tier features it covers.

B) **Sprint-by-sprint table** — for each sprint:
   - Sprint number (continue from 13)
   - Sprint name (3-5 words)
   - Epic
   - Scope (3-5 bullets, concrete deliverables)
   - Dependencies (which sprints must ship first)
   - Lead agent (one of the 5 InkOS leads or a global agent)
   - Estimated complexity (S/M/L/XL based on lessons file: S=1 day, M=2-3 days, L=4-7 days, XL=needs splitting)
   - Risk flags (HIGH/MED/LOW with one-line reason)

C) **Sequencing logic** — explain why epics are ordered the way they are. What blocks what. What can run in parallel.

D) **Refactor sprints baked in** — every 5-7 feature sprints, insert a refactor sprint:
   - Type checker zero-warnings audit
   - Lighthouse performance audit
   - Sage full-codebase review
   - Lesson extraction (run /train)
   - Migration squash check
   These are non-negotiable — production grade requires this cadence.

E) **Quality gates per sprint** — every sprint ends with:
   - pnpm typecheck (zero errors)
   - pnpm build (no warnings)
   - Sage diff audit (zero CRITICAL findings)
   - Luna test pass (new tests for new code)
   - Demo seed regenerated and verified
   - inkos-lessons.md updated if new lesson surfaced

F) **Total sprint count** — give exact number based on the work, not arbitrary 50/100. Likely 60-90.

G) **Critical path** — the sequence of must-ship-first sprints to unlock launch (the Tier 1 list essentially). Estimate calendar weeks at the InkOS factory velocity demonstrated (13 sprints in 2 days per memory — but for production refactor cadence assume 1 sprint = 1-2 days realistic).

H) **Risk register** — top 10 risks with mitigation per risk:
   - Dodo + Stripe dual webhook reconciliation
   - Stripe Connect onboarding friction for non-US studios
   - REACH compliance regulatory drift
   - 1099-NEC vs W-2 misclassification per state
   - Photo timeline storage cost at scale
   - AI Assist hallucination liability
   - Allergy banner false-clear (audit gap)
   - Subdomain DNS ops at scale
   - Migrating existing demo studios to new payment stack
   - Cross-stack feature gate drift (23 keys + new ones)

Be exhaustive. The user wants 50-100 sprints organized so nothing falls through cracks. Better 80 well-organized sprints than 60 ambiguous ones. Output as structured markdown sections, ready for me to drop into a plan file. Target ~3000 words.

DO NOT WRITE CODE. This is roadmap planning only.

1	# InkOS — Project Context for Claude Code
2	
3	> This file is **project-specific only**. Global agent routing, Stack A conventions,
4	> and build standards live in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and are not duplicated here.
5	> If it is unique to InkOS — mission, brand, product model, gotchas — it lives here.
6	> If it applies to every Boldteq Stack A project, it lives in the global file.
7	
8	**Stack:** A (Next.js 16.2.3 + Supabase + Railway + Dodo Payments)
9	**Status:** Sprint 12 complete — launch-ready
10	**Scaffolded by:** Riko on 2026-04-15
11	**Build plan:** `~/.claude/plans/immutable-conjuring-pelican.md` (12 sprints — ALL COMPLETE)
12	**Lessons:** `~/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md` (load on every touch)
13	**Brand Board authority:** `InkOS_Brand_Board.pdf` v1.0 · Locked April 2026
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 1. What InkOS Is
18	
19	**InkOS is the operating system for modern tattoo studios.** Multi-tenant SaaS replacing
20	the fragmented tools (DaySmart / Tattoo Studio Pro / Porter / Fresha / Booksy) that studio
21	owners currently glue together with spreadsheets and Venmo.
22	
23	**Who it's for**
24	- **Studio owners** — running a shop with 1–20 artists, tired of Fresha's 2025 pricing churn,
25	  tired of Porter charging $250 for payroll they rarely use.
26	- **Artists** (resident + guest) — booking clients, managing portfolios, tracking commissions.
27	- **Receptionists** — front-desk booking, consent forms, payments, inventory.
28	
29	**Multi-user from day 1.** No single-seat fallback. Every studio ships with owner +
30	artist + receptionist roles at signup.
31	
32	**Where it runs**
33	- Authenticated web app (no v1 marketing pages — waitlist only at `/`).
34	- Client-facing public booking at `/book/[studioSlug]` (anonymous).
35	- Digital consent forms at `/consent/[token]` (anonymous).
36	- Team invites at `/invite/[token]` (anonymous).
37	
38	**Tagline** (in `app/layout.tsx` metadata):
39	> "The operating system for modern tattoo studios."
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 2. Strategic Moats — Why We Win
44	
45	Five durable advantages from the build plan. Every product/design decision must
46	reinforce at least one of these. If a proposed feature dilutes them, reject it.
47	
48	1. **AI Design Assistant** — Claude-powered moodboards + reference search, included at
49	   Pro ($99). No competitor ships this natively.
50	2. **Full payroll + 1099-K at $99** — Porter charges $250. We commoditize it.
51	3. **EU REACH ink passports + GDPR-native** — First EU-compliant studio OS. Porter and
52	   Fresha are US-first; we ship compliance day 1.
53	4. **Transparent flat pricing** — Post-Fresha 2025 pricing-churn event, studios want
54	   predictable costs. Four tiers, no per-seat surprise fees.
55	5. **Guest artist module at $99** — Porter charges $250 separately. We include it.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## 3. Pricing & Feature Gates (LOCKED)
60	
61	**Four tiers, locked:**
62	
63	| Tier | Price/mo | Positioning |
64	|------|----------|-------------|
65	| Solo | $29 | Single artist, essentials only |
66	| Studio | $59 | Multi-artist operations |
67	| Pro | $99 | AI + payroll + compliance — the anchor tier |
68	| Enterprise | $199 | Multi-location + white-label + API |
69	
70	**Feature-gate source of truth:** [lib/billing/feature-gate.ts](lib/billing/feature-gate.ts) — 23 keys in `KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS`.
71	
72	**Always-on (all tiers, not gated):**
73	`booking` · `calendar` · `public_booking_page` · `digital_consent` · `client_crm` · `dodo_payments` · `custom_domain`
74	
75	**Studio+ (min plan `studio`):**
76	`inventory` · `commissions` · `sms_reminders` · `marketing_basic` · `marketing_advanced` · `calendar_sync` · `referral_program`
77	
78	**Pro+ (min plan `pro`):**
79	`payroll` · `ai_design` · `ai_design_assistant` · `guest_artists` · `eu_reach` · `multi_location` · `analytics`
80	
81	**Enterprise (min plan `enterprise`):**
82	`white_label` · `api_access`
83	
84	**Gating rule (non-negotiable):**
85	- **Server:** API routes call `requireFeatureRpc(supabase, studioId, key)` — throws `FeatureGateError` → 403.
86	- **UI:** Wrap gated components in `<FeatureGate feature="…">` fallback. Never hardcode `plan === 'pro'` checks anywhere.
87	- Dual-layer is mandatory: UI hide + server reject. One layer is a bypass.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## 4. Brand System v1.0 — LOCKED April 2026
92	
93	Source of truth: **InkOS Brand Board v1.0** (PDF) + [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline`.
94	If any design or marketing output breaks this section, Vega / Pixel / Quill / Sage must reject it.
95	
96	### 4.1 Palette — the 60/20/15/5 rule
97	
98	| Color | Hex | Share | Token | Where it appears |
99	|-------|-----|-------|-------|------------------|
100	| **Bone**  | `#F7F7F5` | 60% | `--color-bone` | Page background, sidebar background, card surfaces, empty states. The canvas. |
101	| **Onyx**  | `#0F0F0F` | 20% | `--color-onyx` | Primary text, headlines, KPI numbers, primary CTAs (`+ New booking`), logo, workspace mark. |
102	| **Stone** | `#787774` | 15% | `--color-stone` | Secondary text, labels, metadata, section headers ("STUDIO", "OPERATIONS"), borders. |
103	| **Rust**  | `#B23A2B` | 5%  | `--color-rust` | Active nav state, LIVE pulse, "NOW" sweep bar, accent border on hero KPI, destructive CTA. **Once or twice per viewport max.** |
104	
105	**Forbidden:**
106	- `#FFFFFF` — use Bone `#F7F7F5` instead.
107	- `#000000` — use Onyx `#0F0F0F` instead.
108	- **Any color outside the four above.** No additions. No substitutes. No brand purple, teal,
109	  "accent blue", success green (use Onyx text on Bone bg with a green dot if you must).
110	- Gradients — solid surfaces only.
111	- Raw hex literals in components — always use semantic tokens from `globals.css`.
112	
113	**Semantic derivations** (already wired in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)):
114	`--color-primary` = Onyx · `--color-destructive` = Rust · `--color-accent` = Rust @ 8%
115	opacity · `--color-muted-foreground` = Stone · `--color-border` = Stone-tinted.
116	
117	### 4.2 Typography
118	
119	| Family | Weights | Use |
120	|--------|---------|-----|
121	| **Inter** | 400 / 500 / 600 / 700 / 800 | Everything except display moments. Primary workhorse. |
122	| **Instrument Serif** | 400 roman + italic | Page titles, italic accent words, empty-state names. **Display only.** |
123	| **JetBrains Mono** | 400 / 500 | Code, logs, API responses. Never UI copy. |
124	
125	**Type scale** (all tokens live in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)):
126	
127	| Token | Font | Size | Weight | Use |
128	|-------|------|------|--------|-----|
129	| `display` | Instrument Serif | 52px | 400 | Dashboard hero: *"The studio, at a glance."* |
130	| `page-title` | Instrument Serif | 36px | 400 | Empty-state names: *"Artists & Team"*, *"Calendar"* |
131	| `kpi` | Inter | 52px | 800 | Dashboard numbers: `$8,320`, `87`, `94` |
132	| `h2` | Inter | 24px | 700 | Section titles inside pages |
133	| `h3` | Inter | 16px | 700 | Card titles, list headers |
134	| `body` | Inter | 14px | 400 | Descriptions, paragraphs |
135	| `label` | Inter | 11px | 700 | Uppercase, `tracking-0.08em` — "TODAY'S REVENUE", "STUDIO", "GROWTH" |
136	| `caption` | Inter | 12px | 400 | Metadata, timestamps — *"vs. last Tue"* |
137	
138	**Rules:**
139	- **Tabular figures on every number** (KPIs, prices, counts) — `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.
140	- **Never serif on body text, labels, or data.** Serif is for moments, not paragraphs.
141	- **Italicize emphasis words, never full sentences.** The italic carries tone, not volume.
142	- Example of correct serif use: *"Four colors. Locked."* · *"The signature."* · *"The rules."*
143	
144	### 4.3 Logo & Mark
145	
146	**The mark:** lowercase italic `i` in a filled tile. One shape works at every size.
147	
148	**Lockups:**
149	- **Horizontal** — tile + "InkOS" wordmark + "Studio OS" subtitle (sidebar brandmark, email signature if 24px+).
150	- **Wordmark only** — *i*nkOS (marketing hero where tile would compete).
151	- **Stacked mono** — Onyx tile with Rust `i` + white "InkOS" (dark hero sections, onboarding).
152	
153	**Tile variants:**
154	- `i` on Bone (default, light backgrounds).
155	- `i` on Onyx (dark hero, sidebar expanded, loading states).
156	- `i` on Rust (rare — only for brand-identity moments like favicons on dark mode UAs).
157	
158	**Sizing:**
159	
160	| Context | Size | Notes |
161	|---------|------|-------|
162	| Favicon / app icon | 16–64px | Mark only, no wordmark, no subtitle |
163	| Sidebar brandmark | 32px tile | With wordmark beside + "Studio OS" subtitle below |
164	| Marketing hero | 48px+ tile | Full horizontal lockup |
165	| Email signature | 24px tile | Inline with wordmark only, no subtitle |
166	
167	**Clear space:** padding on all sides ≥ 0.5× tile height. Don't crowd the mark.
168	
169	### 4.4 The 4 Brand Rules (reject anything that breaks these)
170	
171	1. **Editorial polish, not corporate template.**
172	   InkOS looks like a magazine editor built a CRM. Serif italic accents · Bone background
173	   instead of sterile white · restrained color use. **Never** generic SaaS purple. **Never**
174	   Fresha-energetic. **Never** rainbow-gradient landing heroes.
175	
176	2. **Rust is earned, never decorative.**
177	   Every use of `#B23A2B` must answer: *"is this the active state, the live indicator, or
178	   the critical anchor?"* If no — it's not Rust. Use Onyx or Stone instead.
179	
180	3. **Onyx buttons carry the workflow.**
181	   Primary CTAs (`+ New booking`, `Approve`, `Save`) are Onyx, not Rust. Rust CTAs are
182	   reserved for rare destructive-accent moments (`Delete permanently`, `Revoke access`).
183	   Black buttons on Bone = premium B2B. Red everywhere = consumer app.
184	
185	4. **Serif shows up in moments, not paragraphs.**
186	   Instrument Serif is for page titles, italic accent words, empty-state names.
187	   **Never** body text, **never** labels, **never** numbers. Inter carries the workload;
188	   the serif carries the personality.
189	
190	### 4.5 Motion
191	
192	**The "NOW" sweep bar is the only motion on the dashboard.** 2px vertical line + pulsing
193	10px dot, both Rust, sweeping across the current time in `/dashboard` timeline.
194	Nothing else animates on the main dashboard. No spinners on hover. No carousel
195	autoscroll. No confetti. No gradient shifts. Stillness is the brand.
196	
197	Elsewhere: keep motion functional — route transitions, toast slide-in, drawer open.
198	Never decorative. 150ms default, `ease-out`.
199	
200	### 4.6 Shadow tokens (never use default Tailwind shadows)
201	
202	| Token | Use |
203	|-------|-----|
204	| `shadow-soft` | Hairline card borders, inputs |
205	| `shadow-card` | Standard card elevation on Bone |
206	| `shadow-card-hover` | Card hover lift |
207	| `shadow-soft-md` | Drawers, modals |
208	| `shadow-lift` | Command palette, toasts, tooltips |
209	| `shadow-overlay` | Modal backdrops |
210	
211	**Forbidden:** `shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`, `shadow-lg`, `shadow-xl`, `shadow-2xl` — Tailwind defaults are too blue and too heavy for Bone.
212	
213	### 4.7 Do / Don't
214	
215	**DO**
216	- Use Bone as the default page background — everywhere.
217	- Pair Onyx headlines with Stone subtitles for quiet hierarchy.
218	- Reserve Rust for one or two elements per viewport.
219	- Use Instrument Serif only on page titles + italic emphasis.
220	- Keep the "NOW" sweep bar as the only motion on the dashboard.
221	- Use tabular figures on every number (KPIs, prices, counts).
222	
223	**DON'T**
224	- Add any color outside Bone / Rust / Stone / Onyx.
225	- Use Rust as a button background (except rare destructive).
226	- Italicize full sentences — emphasis words only.
227	- Use Instrument Serif on body text, labels, or data.
228	- Use pure white (`#FFFFFF`) — always Bone.
229	- Use pure black (`#000000`) — always Onyx.
230

232	
233	## 5. UI Philosophy (how every screen is built)
234	
235	- **Solid surfaces only** — no gradients, no glassmorphism, no frosted blur.
236	- **Hairline Stone borders** — `--color-border` at Stone-tinted opacity. No heavy strokes.
237	- **Light mode default.** Dark mode is theme-toggle secondary — honor tokens but don't design dark-first.
238	- **KPI cards** — Onyx number (Inter 800, tabular), Stone label (uppercase, tracked `0.08em`),
239	  optional Rust 2px left border on the single hero KPI per viewport.
240	- **One Rust accent per viewport, maximum two.** If you need a third, you're designing wrong.
241	- **All tokens live in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline`** — Tailwind 4, no `tailwind.config.ts`, ever.
242	- **Spacing** — page padding `1.5rem` desktop / `1rem` mobile; card padding `1.5rem`; section gap `1.5rem`.
243	- **Sidebar** — `16rem` desktop (S24, was `15rem`), `19rem` mobile drawer, `3.5rem` icon-mode. Bone background, Rust active state at 8% opacity. Keep CSS vars (`--sidebar-width*` in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)) in lockstep with JS constants in [components/ui/sidebar.tsx](components/ui/sidebar.tsx) — SidebarProvider writes them as inline styles, so drift silently breaks collapse transitions.
244	
245	---
246	
247	## 6. Voice & Copy — Quill Reference
248	
249	**Tone:** editorial, quiet, confident. Never hype. Never exclamation marks. Never "Amazing!".
250	
251	**Cadence:** short sentences. Periods, not commas, carry rhythm. Italics earn their place.
252	
253	**Examples of correct display copy (from the brand board):**
254	- *"The studio, at a glance."*
255	- *"Today's schedule — Tuesday, April 21 · noon–midnight"*
256	- *"Six chairs running. One guest from Mumbai. Three bookings flagged for a gentle nudge."*
257	- *"The brand, in full."*
258	- *"Four colors. Locked."*
259	
260	**Numbers stand alone.** `$8,320` · `87%` · `94` — Inter 800, tabular, no decorative prefix.
261	
262	**Microcopy rules:**
263	- Primary CTA verbs: "Book", "Save", "Send", "Approve". Not "Click here", not "Submit".
264	- Empty states: serif name + one-sentence editorial explanation. No illustrations with shrug emojis.
265	- Error messages: factual, no "Oops!". Example: *"Deposit couldn't be processed. The card was declined by the issuer."*
266	- Email subject lines: no emojis, no ALL CAPS, no "🔥 Last chance!".
267	
268	Quill owns marketing landing / email / social / in-app microcopy.
269	Pixel owns the 14 public-page copy structures under Quill's voice.
270	
271	---
272	
273	## 7. Architecture Decisions (project-specific)
274	
275	1. **Next.js 16 uses `proxy.ts` not `middleware.ts`** — at project root, not in `app/`.
276	2. **`cookies()` is async in Next 16** — always `await cookies()`.
277	3. **Worker packages NEVER import `next/*`** — separate `package.json` in `workers/jobs/` and `workers/cron/`.
278	4. **BullMQ ioredis requires `maxRetriesPerRequest: null`** — silent failure without it.
279	5. **Supabase service-role client bypasses RLS** — only in webhook handlers + admin ops.
280	6. **Webhook handler uses `timingSafeEqual`** — constant-time HMAC comparison, never `===`.
281	7. **`subscriptions` table is write-only by webhook** — no app code writes to it directly.
282	8. **Tailwind 4 — no `tailwind.config.ts`** — all tokens in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline` only.
283	
284	---
285	
286	## 8. Forbidden (Sage hard-fails on review)
287	
288	- `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` — use `@supabase/ssr`
289	- Vercel — use Railway
290	- Stripe — use Dodo Payments
291	- NextAuth — use Supabase Auth
292	- Prisma / any ORM — use Supabase client + generated types
293	- Pages Router — App Router only
294	- npm / yarn — pnpm only
295	- CSS modules — Tailwind only
296	- `any` TypeScript — zero exceptions
297	- `console.log` — use [lib/logger.ts](lib/logger.ts) (pino)
298	- **Raw hex literals in components** — use tokens from `globals.css`. Only `globals.css` itself defines hexes, and only for Bone / Onyx / Stone / Rust.
299	- `tailwind.config.ts` — Tailwind 4 lives in `@theme inline` only.
300	- Default Tailwind shadows (`shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`, etc.) — use `shadow-soft` / `shadow-card` / `shadow-soft-md`.
301	- Hardcoded plan-tier checks (`plan === 'pro'`) — use `hasFeature(plan, key)` or `<FeatureGate>`.
302	- Hand-edits to [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts) — regenerate with `pnpm db:types`.
303	
304	---
305	
306	## 9. Recurring Antipatterns (from `inkos-lessons.md`)
307	
308	Load `~/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md` on every touch. The traps we keep hitting:
309	
310	- **Never hand-edit [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts)** — always `pnpm db:types` after any Dato migration.

11	# InkOS Build Lessons
12	
13	## 1. Recurring Sage Findings — Systematic Pipeline Weaknesses
14	
15	### 1A. RPC Parameter Mismatches (Dato writes RPC, Koda writes route with different params)
16	
17	Appeared in Sprint 5 (C1: camelCase `submissionId` vs snake_case `submission_id` in consent PDF job), Sprint 6 (C1: `public_get_invite_by_token` vs `get_invite_by_token`; C2: `accept_team_invite` missing `artist_id` and `commission_default_pct` in return shape), Sprint 7 (M1: `applied_date` vs `applied_at`), and Sprint 8 (S8#1: `set_artist_tax_info` param mismatch). Root cause: Dato writes the migration defining the RPC signature, Koda writes the API route consuming it, and neither verifies the other's contract. The hand-written `lib/supabase/types.ts` masks the drift because TypeScript trusts whatever is manually typed. **Prevention rule:** Before Koda writes any route that calls an RPC, the RPC's exact parameter names and return fields must be extracted from the migration SQL into a shared TypeScript interface. If Dato and Koda run in parallel, the contract must be defined in the design spec as a shared interface BEFORE either starts coding.
18	
19	### 1B. Column Name Drift (migration says X, types say Y, code says Z)
20	
21	Appeared in Sprint 1 (C3: `locations` migration missing `zip`/`phone` that types declared), Sprint 3 (C2: `sort_order` column missing from migration but code referenced it), Sprint 6 (C3: `studio_members.last_active_at` not in migration but in types), Sprint 7 (M1: `applied_date` vs `applied_at`), Sprint 8-12 audit (S11#8: `status` column on `marketing_campaigns` missing, S12#12: `payroll_items` table referenced but doesn't exist). Root cause: `lib/supabase/types.ts` was hand-edited throughout the build instead of regenerated from the actual DB schema. **Prevention rule:** Never hand-edit the types file. After every Dato migration, run `pnpm supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts`. If the Supabase project doesn't exist yet (as in InkOS), maintain a strict convention: Dato writes the migration, Dato updates types to exactly match, and Koda does NOT touch the types file. Any column referenced in code must exist in the migration first.
22	
23	### 1C. `asChild` Violations on base-nova
24	
25	Every Sage audit checked for `asChild` usage on base-nova (shadcn/ui's `@base-ui-components/react`) components. In InkOS this passed cleanly because it was caught early (Sprint 1 scan), but the automated grep for `asChild` was added to every single audit because this is a known recurring problem across Boldteq builds. **Rule:** All components from base-nova use the `render` prop pattern, never `asChild`. This must be in every project's ESLint config as a custom rule or at minimum in the Sage automated scan.
26	
27	### 1D. Missing Rate Limits on GET Endpoints
28	
29	Sprint 1 (M1: auth rate limits architecturally impossible), Sprint 6 (public invite route needed rate limit), Sprint 8-12 combined audit (cross-sprint #17: payroll GET routes missing rate limits). Koda consistently forgets rate limits on read routes, treating them as "safe." But unbounded GETs enable enumeration, scraping, and DoS. **Rule:** Every API route, GET or POST, must import and call either `authedRatelimit` or `publicBookingReadRatelimit` before any DB query. Sage scans for routes missing rate-limit calls.
30	
31	### 1E. `onValueChange` Null Guards for base-ui Select
32	
33	Not specific to InkOS (passed here) but flagged as a check item in every audit. When base-ui Select fires `onValueChange`, the value can be `null` on deselect. Without a guard, the handler crashes or sends null to the API. **Rule:** Every `onValueChange` handler must check `if (value === null) return` before processing.
34	
35	### 1F. `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` Violations
36	
37	Sprint 4 build report (item #2): interface optionals needed `| undefined` suffix. Throughout the build, Koda hit TypeScript errors where `{ field?: string }` doesn't accept `undefined` under strict optional property types. **Rule:** Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, always declare optional fields as `field?: string | undefined` in interfaces. Or better: use Zod schema inference (`z.infer<typeof Schema>`) which handles this automatically.
38	
39	### 1G. Feature Gate Key Mismatches
40	
41	Sprint 7 (C1): the plans JSONB in the billing migration used `commission_splits` but all code used `commissions`. Today's static `requireFeature()` compares plan order (not JSONB keys), so it accidentally worked. But if anyone switches to the RPC-based `requireFeatureRpc()` (which reads JSONB), all gates 403. **Rule:** Define all feature gate keys in a single `lib/billing/feature-keys.ts` constant. Both the migration seed data and the `requireFeature()` callers import from this file. Drift is a compile error instead of a runtime surprise.
42	
43	### 1H. Public Routes Using Session Client Instead of Anon
44	
45	Sprint 5 (C6, C7): public consent pages imported `createClient` from `@/lib/supabase/server` (session-cookie client) instead of `createPublicClient`. Functional today (RPC grants to anon) but leaks the logged-in user's session into a public route. **Rule:** Every route under `/book/`, `/consent/`, `/invite/`, or `/api/public/` must use `createPublicClient()` from `@/lib/supabase/public`. Sage grepping for `createClient` in public routes is now a mandatory scan.
46	
47	### 1I. `unstable_cache` Capturing Authenticated Clients
48	
49	Sprint 7 (M3): `unstable_cache(async () => supabase.rpc(...))` captured the first caller's authenticated client. Subsequent requests within the cache TTL reuse the first caller's JWT. **Rule:** Never wrap `supabase.rpc()` calls in `unstable_cache` when the supabase client is session-scoped. Cache the RESULT of the RPC call (a plain object), not the client invocation. Or just don't use `unstable_cache` for authenticated data -- it's not worth the footgun.
50	
51	## 2. Sprint Velocity Patterns — What Worked for Parallel Execution
52	
53	### 2A. Dato + Vega in Parallel (No Dependency)
54	
55	Dato writes the migration (schema, RPCs, RLS, triggers) while Vega writes the design spec (UI layout, component hierarchy, interaction patterns). These have zero dependencies. Starting them in parallel saves 2-4 hours per sprint. Koda then consumes BOTH outputs to build the API routes and UI.
56	
57	### 2B. Sage Audit in Background While Next Sprint Starts
58	
59	After Koda delivers a sprint, Sage audits the output while Dato and Vega start on the next sprint. The next sprint's Koda build can begin on features that don't overlap with the audit scope. This pipeline parallelism was critical for shipping 13 sprints in 2 days. Exception: if Sage's audit is BLOCK severity, the fix Koda must run before proceeding.
60	
61	### 2C. Fix Koda + Build Koda Can Run in Parallel If File Scopes Don't Overlap
62	
63	When Sage flags fixes in Sprint N, a "fix Koda" agent addresses those while a "build Koda" agent starts Sprint N+1's non-overlapping files. This worked well when Sprint 3 fixes (client CRM) ran alongside Sprint 4 scaffold (billing). Does NOT work when the fix touches shared infrastructure like `lib/supabase/types.ts` or `lib/supabase/server.ts`.
64	
65	### 2D. API 500 Errors Recovered by Checking Partial State
66	
67	When a sprint's build partially failed (e.g., missing column caused a 500), Yash dispatched a fix agent that first checked what was already built and correct, then surgically fixed only the broken parts. Avoids the temptation to rewrite entire files.
68	
69	### 2E. Batch Sage Audits Are Worse Than Per-Sprint Audits
70	
71	Sprints 8-12 were batched into one combined Sage audit. This found 4 critical issues that had been compounding for 5 sprints. Per-sprint audits (Sprints 1-7) caught issues immediately, before they could cascade. **Rule:** Run Sage after EVERY sprint, not batched. The 30-minute audit cost per sprint is cheaper than the 4-hour compound fix session.
72	
73	## 3. Architecture Decisions That Proved Right
74	
75	### 3A. RPC-Only Writes for Audit-Critical Tables
76	
77	`consent_form_submissions` has zero direct-write RLS policies -- all writes go through `submit_consent_form` RPC. `commission_records` same pattern. This means: (a) business logic (snapshot creation, audit hash, penalty generation) can't be bypassed; (b) the RPC is the single source of truth for mutation semantics; (c) RLS stays simple (just read policies). **Apply to:** Any table where data integrity is a legal or financial obligation (consent, pay, billing, audit logs).
78	
79	### 3B. `EXCLUDE USING gist` for Booking Conflicts
80	
81	The `bookings_artist_no_overlap` exclusion constraint catches double-bookings at the DB level. Every write path (API route, public RPC, admin override) that creates/moves a booking is automatically protected. Without this, every write path would need its own conflict-check query, and one would inevitably be missed. Effort to set up: 5 lines of SQL. Effort saved: hours of bug-hunting. **Apply to:** Any domain with time-range conflicts (schedules, reservations, resource allocation).
82	
83	### 3C. `GENERATED ALWAYS` Columns for Computed Values
84	
85	`bookings.end_at` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (scheduled_at + (duration_min || ' minutes')::interval) STORED`. This means `end_at` can never drift from `scheduled_at + duration`. No code path can accidentally set a wrong `end_at`. Sage verified this by grepping for `end_at` in INSERT/UPDATE payloads -- zero hits. **Apply to:** Any column that's a deterministic function of other columns (totals, dates, durations).
86	
87	### 3D. Feature Gate Server-Enforced + UI-Hidden (Dual Enforcement)
88	
89	Every gated feature has: (1) `requireFeature(plan, 'key')` in the API route that returns 403, AND (2) `featureKey` in the sidebar nav-config that hides the link AND (3) `<UpgradeGate>` component that shows a blur overlay. Three layers means a user can never reach a paid feature through URL manipulation, deep linking, or API probing. **Apply to:** Every SaaS with tiered plans.
90	
91	### 3E. Worker-Only for Expensive Operations
92	
93	AI design generation (Claude + DALL-E pipeline), PDF generation (react-pdf/renderer), and low-stock email alerts all run in BullMQ workers, never in API routes. This prevents: request timeouts, memory pressure on the web process, and blocking other requests. **Apply to:** Any operation that takes >5s or uses >100MB memory.
94	
95	## 4. Architecture Decisions That Caused Problems
96	
97	### 4A. Hand-Written `lib/supabase/types.ts`
98	
99	This was the single largest source of bugs across the entire build. Every sprint had at least one finding traceable to types not matching the migration. The types file was 3000+ lines of manually maintained TypeScript that drifted from reality. **Fix for future builds:** Use `pnpm supabase gen types typescript` after every migration. If the Supabase project doesn't exist yet, use `supabase start` locally and generate from the local DB. Never hand-edit.

## C) Sequencing Logic

**Why epics are ordered this way:**

1. **Epic 1 (Stripe Connect) ships first** because every later money-touching feature (deposit pool in portal S34, flash deposit-gate S49, lifecycle credits S43, multi-currency S67, apprentice splits S73, dispute packs S86) depends on the new payment rail. Building any of those before Connect lands means rework.
2. **Epic 2 (AI Assist) before Epic 3 (Client Safety)** because the inbound-reply-draft job lives in inbox UI that Epic 2 also rebuilds — building portal first would force a second pass on inbox.
3. **Epic 3 (Allergies + Portal + Briefing + Financial)** is the launch-blocker tier completion — these four sprints close the Tier 1 list. Critical path ends at S37.
4. **Epic 4 (Sessions table promotion)** runs after launch-critical because it's a data-shape migration; doing it earlier risks losing Tier 1 velocity.
5. **Epic 5 (Public surface)** depends on portal foundation (S33) and brand pass (S38), and unblocks Enterprise custom domain (S47 → S60+).
6. **Epic 6 (Compliance/Tax/Analytics)** depends on payments + sessions; tax sub-ledger needs Connect, REACH fail-fast needs sessions table.
7. **Epic 7 (Enterprise)** depends on multi-location data shapes from Epic 6 (#57).
8. **Epic 8 (i18n + multi-currency)** is intentionally after Enterprise because cross-border Connect needs Connect at maturity.
9. **Epic 9 (Workforce + Onboarding)** depends on every prior epic — onboarding wizard touches Connect, brand, license, BBP, tax.
10. **Epic 10 (Hardening)** is the penultimate epic by design — you can't harden until features are complete; doing it earlier means re-hardening every sprint.
11. **Epic 11 (Brand/Demo/PDF/DR)** is the final polish layer. Demo personas must reflect the *finished* product, not a moving target.

**What can run in parallel:**
- S13 (schema) ‖ S14 (webhook wiring) once Dato finalizes RPC signatures.
- S19 (Stripe Tax) ‖ S14–S18 since tax matrix is independent of charge flow.
- S26 (consult summary) ‖ S25 (reply drafts) — independent AI jobs.
- S39 (sessions table) ‖ S40 (photo slots) only if Dato writes both migrations cleanly.
- S46 (subdomain) ‖ S48 (kiosk) — different surfaces.
- S60 (white-label) ‖ S61–S63 (API) — can fan out.
- S68 (i18n) ‖ S69 (fr/de copy) once locale shells exist.

**What blocks what (hard dependency edges):**
- S13 → everything in Epic 1.
- S22 (refactor gate) → Epic 2 start.
- S37 → Epic 4 start (sessions migration on stable foundation).
- S39 → S40 → S41 → S42 → S43 → S44 (lifecycle is sequential).
- S65 (feature-key wiring) → Epic 7 launchable.

## D) Refactor Sprints — Baked In, Non-Negotiable

Refactor sprints fire **every 5–7 feature sprints**. Each refactor sprint:

- **Type checker zero-warnings audit** — `pnpm typecheck` zero errors AND zero warnings; `lib/supabase/types.ts` regenerated with `pnpm db:types`.
- **Lighthouse performance audit** — every changed route checked; LCP <2.5s, CLS <0.1, INP <200ms; regressions blocked.
- **Sage full-codebase review** — diff-mode against last refactor checkpoint; CRITICAL findings blocking; HIGH findings tracked.
- **Lesson extraction** — `/train` runs against the last 5–7 sprints; updates `~/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md`.
- **Migration squash check** — ensure no orphan migrations, no skipped numbers, all RPCs have shared TS interfaces, types regenerated.

**Refactor sprint locations:** S22, S31, S37, S45, S52, S59, S66, S71, S77, S83. (10 refactor sprints embedded; Epic 11 ends with S87 final-DR which functions as the pre-launch hardening checkpoint.)

## E) Quality Gates — Every Sprint Ends With

These run in the same order, every single sprint, no exceptions:

1. **`pnpm typecheck`** — zero errors.
2. **`pnpm build`** — zero warnings.
3. **Sage diff audit** — zero CRITICAL findings; HIGH findings logged with explicit defer rationale.
4. **Luna test pass** — new tests for new code (unit + integration where applicable + Playwright for any new public flow).
